name: greymicroagent port policy

greymicroagent.port_block: 7640-7647 — owner 2026-11-17: completely unique ports never used by anything else; verified free against every port_policy.json and every live listener; below the Linux ephemeral range so the kernel never auto-assigns them
greymicroagent.lane_kind: slimtoken — client-side in-front filter (brain traffic only)
greymicroagent.model_file: ~/.greymicroagent/models/qwen3-vl-2b-abliterated.gguf (symlink to the immutable ollama store blob); classic 2B/4B ggufs stay linked beside it

other_families_off_limits.11600: cloud ollama direct — no listener, proxy, or interceptor ever; direct calls only
other_families_off_limits.11434: ollama local — dead forever; never resurrect; no loggers
other_families_off_limits.11435: cortexagent-cloud + Claude Code shared CLOUD lane (owner 2026-10-25: one lane for all cloud harnesses) — another family's lane
other_families_off_limits.11436: cortexagent local slimtoken proxy — another family's lane
other_families_off_limits.11598: RETIRED 2026-10-24 (unit disabled; upstream :11599 dead) — dead forever, never resurrect
other_families_off_limits.11599: cortexagent local llama-server — the RAW model port itself, NOT a slimtoken lane
other_families_off_limits.4444-4447, 4454-4457: greymini's own historic expansion pairs — left behind entirely; this fork no longer claims them
other_families_off_limits.7080, 7081: another family's primary pair — left behind entirely

shared_local_infra.8888: local SearXNG (self-hosted; greymicroagent's search stack may use it)

rules: greymicroagent session slots are 2 live triples (7640,7641,7642) and (7643,7644,7645), each slot a model:lane:slimtoken triple inside its own unique 7640-7647 block, with 7646-7647 held as spare expansion for a future third session; every port of the block is owned by this fork only
port occupied by anything else = plain refusal or documented direct fallback, never a fight
lanes are client-side in-front filters of their own upstream only — never listeners on foreign ports
cleanup kills captured pids/process groups only — never name-pattern sweeps (greymicroagent-server is a fork-unique name so foreign kill sweeps cannot touch it)
